messages:
laura: Heads-up: trying to wire the TS SDK into a Next.js middleware (Edge) and hitting weird build-time tree-shaking that pulls in `crypto.randomBytes` even though I only use the /edge import.
dan: Which path did you import? we published `redwood-inference/edge` specifically to avoid node shims.
laura: import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge' — still the bundle had a reference to crypto in the final lambda bytecount. Build log shows `require('crypto')` from a transitive util.
marco: Oof, that happens when rollup/webpack statically resolves conditional requires. Did you lock to the new 2.3.1 edge release? we added conditional exports to prevent that.
laura: Oh I'm on 2.2.9. Upgrading now...
laura: After upgrade the build passes. Runtime though: Next's middleware gives me a NextRequest not the standard Request; `request.json()` works but `new Headers(request.headers)` returns a Headers with lowercase keys only. SDK code that checks `headers.get('x-user-id')` fails sometimes.
praveen: NextRequest headers is a Headers object but the edge platform canonicalizes header names. The fix is to use `request.headers.get('x-user-id')` not indexing or to normalize keys.
dan: Another subtlety: AbortController/AbortSignal exists but `AbortSignal.timeout()` is not available on the platform. If SDK calls that we'll crash. We had to guard: `if (typeof AbortSignal?.timeout === 'function')` before using.
marco: Also add a platform check for `globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues`. Node's `crypto.randomBytes` won't be present. We polyfilled a tiny uuid helper that uses getRandomValues when available and falls back to a weak counter otherwise for telemetry IDs in edge.
laura: Good note. Anything on typings? TS complains about `NextRequest` mismatch with lib.dom Request in our middleware handler signatures.
praveen: For DX we added this snippet to the docs: ```ts
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'
export function middleware(req: NextRequest) {
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  // cast REQUEST to any when calling SDK if needed:
  return client.generate({ prompt: 'x' })
}
``` It explains the casting tradeoff and suggests adding `skipLibCheck` for quickstarts.
dan: Filed a small RFC to add an explicit `types/edge.d.ts` in the SDK that exports helper overloads accepting NextRequest. If we ship that, devs won't need casts.
marco: CI update: ci-bot created a matrix job `edge-next-middleware` that runs a minimal Next app build on Node 20 + Vercel adapter. It runs smoke e2e for middleware sample.
ci-bot: CI job `edge-next-middleware` queued on branch `sdk/edge-guardrails` (PR #782).
laura: One last pitfall for anyone reading later: avoid importing `crypto` anywhere in files under `app/middleware` or `middleware` because Vercel still flags it even if unused. Put node-only utilities under `lib/server` and import only inside server routes.
praveen: I'll add a short checklist in the README: /edge entrypoint, avoid node cores, prefer `globalThis.crypto`, guard AbortSignal.timeout, NextRequest overloads.
laura: Thanks — that would've saved me an hour. :relieved:
